_about: Content for the Read-more screens (PlaceStoryScreen) of Discover Bremen. Texts are short B1-English drafts, checked against the sources listed per place. Mohamad rewrites them in his own words before submission. Photos: Unsplash License (free to use, attribution not required; the app shows credits anyway). Distances: straight line between Wikipedia coordinates, rounded to 50 m.
photo_url_params: Each photo url already asks for a 1200 px wide JPEG (auto=format&fit=crop&w=1200&q=75). Keep these parameters.

places.name: Bremen Town Musicians
places.about: A bronze statue of the four animals from the Grimm tale, standing on each other’s backs. It is about 2 m tall and stands at the west side of the Town Hall.
places.story: The Brothers Grimm published the tale in 1819. The animals never reach Bremen: they find a robbers’ house and stay there. Gerhard Marcks made the statue. It was put up in 1953, first as a one-year trial.
places.tradition: Hold both front legs of the donkey and make a wish. Locals say that one hand on one leg shows you are new in Bremen.

visit.address: Schoppensteel, west side of the Town Hall, 28195 Bremen

places.name: Schlachte
places.about: A 660 m promenade on the Weser in the old town. Restaurants and bars line the quay, next to old ships such as the Alexander von Humboldt.
places.story: The name comes from Low German slagte: the posts driven into the river bank. From the 13th century this was Bremen’s harbour. In the 19th century the railway and new port basins took over. From 1993 to 2000 the quay was rebuilt as a promenade.
places.tradition: In winter the Schlachte-Zauber market fills the quay with about 100 wooden huts and lit-up ships, from late November to December.

places.name: Schnoor Quarter
places.about: Bremen’s oldest quarter: narrow lanes with small houses, shops and cafés. Some lanes are so narrow that you can touch both walls with your arms.
places.story: Fishermen, boatmen and craftsmen lived here by the Balge, an arm of the Weser. “Schnoor” means string or cord in Low German and comes from the old ship trades. The oldest house, Schnoor 2, is from 1401. Many houses were restored from 1955 on.
places.tradition: Look for the Katzengang, a very narrow lane. At the Bremer Bonbon Manufaktur you can watch sweets being made by hand.

visit.access: Open-air, any time. Shops have their own hours.

places.name: St. Petri Cathedral
places.about: Bremen’s Protestant cathedral, next to the Marktplatz. Its two west towers are about 93 m high, and 265 steps lead up the south tower.
places.story: A church stood here from about 789. The oldest parts you can still see, the crypts, are from the 11th century. In the Bleikeller, eight mummified bodies lie in coffins that you can look into.
places.tradition: Unmarried men who turn 30 sweep the cathedral steps while friends watch. They may stop when a “virgin” kisses them. Unmarried women polish the door handles instead. The custom goes back to about 1890.

visit.price: Dom-Museum free. Tower and Bleikeller: check prices.
visit.access: Check opening times. Tower and Bleikeller are seasonal.

checks_of_existing_app_texts.text: Grimm fairy tale, 1819. Bronze statue by Gerhard Marcks (1953), right next to the Town Hall — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the Roland since 2004.
“Schnoor” means string in Low German: the tiny houses stand in a row like pearls on a string. Many date from the 15th to the 18th century.
checks_of_existing_app_texts.note: bremen.eu uses the 'pearls on a string' picture; Wikipedia explains the name with the old ship crafts (cord). Oldest house 1401, many houses from the 17th and 18th century.

checks_of_existing_app_texts.text: Parts of the cathedral date back to the 11th century. Don't miss the Bleikeller, a cellar with mummified bodies.
For centuries, ships unloaded their goods here. Today the quay is lined with restaurants and old ships, and it is lively on summer evenings.
checks_of_existing_app_texts.note: 'lively on summer evenings' is an opinion, not a fact.
